chapters.title: Everything is vapor
chapters.summary: The Teacher says everything is vanity, a breath. Generations come and go, the sun rises and sets, and there is nothing new under the sun.

chapters.title: The search for meaning
chapters.summary: The Teacher tries pleasure, great projects and wealth, and finds it all like chasing the wind. Even the wise die like fools.

chapters.title: A time for everything
chapters.summary: There is a time for every purpose under heaven. God has made everything beautiful in its time and set eternity in the human heart.

chapters.title: Two are better than one
chapters.summary: Oppression and envy trouble the Teacher. Two are better than one, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

chapters.title: Guard your steps
chapters.summary: Come to God ready to listen, and keep your vows. Lovers of money are never satisfied; enjoy your work as God's gift.

chapters.title: Unsatisfied desire
chapters.summary: Some have wealth but cannot enjoy it. Who knows what is good for a person in this brief life?

chapters.title: Better than
chapters.summary: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the house of mourning teaches more than the house of feasting. In prosperity rejoice; in adversity consider.

chapters.title: Who knows?
chapters.summary: Obey the king. Though the wicked seem to escape, it will be well with those who fear God. No one can understand all God's work.

chapters.title: Enjoy life
chapters.summary: The same end comes to all. Eat your bread with joy, love your spouse, and whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might.

chapters.title: A little folly
chapters.summary: A little foolishness spoils wisdom like dead flies in perfume. Sayings about rulers, work and careful speech.

chapters.title: Cast your bread
chapters.summary: Cast your bread upon the waters and give generously. Rejoice in your youth, but remember God will bring you into judgment.

chapters.title: Remember your Creator
chapters.summary: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before old age comes. The conclusion: fear God and keep His commandments.
